slides.title: Home loan prepayment vs SIP: Which is a better option and saves you more money? Here's the maths
The Core Dilemma
slides.content: When you take a home loan, you commit to paying Equated Monthly Installments (EMIs) over a long period. Choosing where to put extra cash creates a tough choice between clearing debt or growing investments.

slides.title: The Tenure Factor
slides.label: Year Loan Tenure
slides.context: Home loans are commonly spread over a span of 20 to 25 years, meaning interest builds up substantially over the life of the loan.

steps.text: Target the initial years of the loan
Significantly reduce overall interest outgoings over time

slides.title: Prepayment vs SIP Realities
slides.left_text: Guaranteed savings by lowering the principal amount and cutting future interest costs.
slides.right_text: Investing fixed amounts regularly into mutual funds with variable market returns.

items.text: Lower total interest burden with early loan reductions
Immediate liquidity reduction if cash goes to the bank
Potential market wealth creation via SIPs instead of debt closure

slides.title: Remaining Uncertainties
slides.content: Market returns from an SIP are never guaranteed, whereas loan interest rates can fluctuate. Your final choice depends on your personal comfort with risk and your specific loan terms.
